title: Make documentation review issue-scoped and advisory on existing drift
description:
Change the AI documentation review gate from a default full-surface audit into an issue-scoped documentation-impact review. The reviewer reconstructs the implementation footprint from commits tagged for the context issue, checks the smallest documentation impact cone—including required but untouched docs—and enforces concise user-facing prose without allowing unrelated existing drift to block delivery.

## Background

The adopter-facing documentation surface has completed a comprehensive audit. Repeating that audit whenever `doc-review` runs creates noise and makes unrelated drift gate-blocking. Commit messages already carry `jit:<short-id>` tags, which give the reviewer an attributable implementation footprint even when issue commits are interleaved with unrelated work.

The issue-scoped review must still catch omitted documentation: touched documentation files alone are not a sufficient scope. Existing drift encountered during review remains useful signal, but it is advisory and does not affect the verdict.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The documentation reviewer discovers commits on the current branch whose messages contain the context issue tag `jit:<short-id>` and constructs the implementation footprint from the union of those individual commit patches, including renames and deletions, rather than from one broad earliest-commit-to-HEAD range that can absorb unrelated commits.
- [hard] REQ-02: When no tagged commit is available, the review falls back to the issue description, success criteria, and linked documents, and states that commit-based attribution was unavailable; uncommitted changes are not automatically attributed to the issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: The reviewer derives the smallest documentation impact cone from the attributable implementation footprint and issue intent. It reviews documentation changed by the issue, documentation that must change because of the issue even when untouched, and links or neighboring text directly affected by those changes.
- [hard] REQ-04: A finding blocks only when it has a direct causal relationship to the issue work, including a missing required documentation update, an inaccurate issue-authored update, or an issue-introduced link, citation, example, placement, discoverability, or material concision defect.
- [hard] REQ-05: Existing unrelated drift encountered during the review is explicitly classified as pre-existing advisory feedback, is recommended to be surfaced without requiring an exhaustive search, and never changes a passing verdict to failure.
- [hard] REQ-06: The review rubric requires concise documentation: direct present-tense statements, focused examples, links to canonical reference material instead of duplication, and omission of implementation history or internal mechanics that users do not need. Material duplication or obscured instructions in issue-authored prose is blocking; sentence-level style preferences are advisory.
- [hard] REQ-07: Structured gate findings preserve whether each finding is blocking or advisory and whether it is issue-impact or pre-existing; a passing structured result may contain advisory findings, and parser/serialization tests cover the new fields and compatibility with findings that omit them.
- [hard] REQ-08: The `doc-review` gate description and reviewer prompt state the issue-scoped policy, commit-tag footprint construction, advisory existing-drift policy, verdict rule, and concise-style rubric consistently; regression coverage verifies the policy-defining prompt content.

## Notes

The verdict rule is: fail if and only if at least one unresolved issue-impact blocking finding exists. Existing-drift findings never fail the gate.

The likely implementation footprint includes `scripts/doc-review-prompt.md`, `.jit/gates.toml`, structured gate-finding domain/output types, and their tests. The implementation may choose stable field names for the two classifications, provided both survive parsing, storage, and JSON output.
